title: Training speedups via batching for geometric learning: an analysis of static and dynamic algorithms
experiments_summary: Timing and learning experiments were conducted using two molecular/material datasets (QM9 and AFLOW), three GNN models (SchNet, MPEU, PaiNN), and four batch sizes (16, 32, 64, 128). Four batching algorithms were evaluated: static-constant, static-2N, static-64, and dynamic. Datasets were converted to graphs (QM9 via full node connectivity; AFLOW via 24-nearest-neighbor KNN). Experiments were run for two million training steps (with additional shorter runs at 100,000 steps), and each algorithm-model-dataset-batch size combination was repeated ten times to reduce hardware noise. Timing was measured using Python's time library with GPU synchronization barriers, capturing mean batching time, mean gradient-update step time, and their sum (combined time). Batch statistics (node/edge distributions before and after padding) were analyzed over 10,000 batches. The number of JAX recompilations per algorithm and batch size was recorded. Hardware used was a single CPU core and single NVIDIA A100 GPU (with additional CPU-only and 4-GPU pmap experiments reported in appendices). To assess learning effects, test RMSE curves were averaged over ten runs per configuration, and pairwise Student's t-tests were performed on final test RMSE distributions across batching algorithms, with p-value thresholds of 0.05 and 0.10 used to judge statistical significance.
